subtype: Approach: writing observations in a daily notebook [Action]
passage: Every morning before brushing his teeth, Devang carried a steel ruler to the balcony. He held it beside the bean plant, read the number, and wrote it in a green notebook under the date: 3 June, 4 cm. On the ninth day his sister Dilnaz peered over his shoulder. "You're only writing numbers." "That's the point," Devang said. "See, a tiny change on day five, then a big jump." Three weeks later he copied the dates and heights onto chart paper. The line climbed slowly with one flat stretch, but every dot on it was something he had really measured.

qa.q: What did Devang write in his green notebook each morning?
qa.a: He wrote the plant's height under the date.

qa.q: What does Devang's reply to Dilnaz suggest about how he feels about the daily notes?
qa.a: He feels quietly proud and sure that the plain numbers matter, because he points to the jump they reveal.

qa.q: What could Devang add to his notebook habit in case he misses a morning, and why?
qa.a: He could take a photo of the plant beside the ruler each day, so a missing note can be checked against a picture.

qa.q: How does Dilnaz see the notebook at first?
qa.a: She sees only a list of numbers, as her remark shows, and has not yet noticed the jump that Devang can point to.

grounding: A boy measures a plant every morning and dates each note, so his final chart holds real numbers.

subtype: Approach: writing observations in a daily notebook [Action]
passage:
"Raghav, why are you on the balcony at six?"
"Measuring, Salma didi."
"Measuring what?"
"My bean plant. Every morning, same time, same ruler."
She peered at his notebook. Rows of dates. 3rd: 2 cm. 4th: 2.5 cm. 5th: 3.5 cm.
"Why write it all down? You can just see it's growing."
"Seeing isn't numbers. At the fair they'll ask how much it grew, and when. If I don't write it, I'll be guessing."
"Why the same time?"
"So it's fair. Plants grow more in some hours."
On fair day, Raghav's line graph went up in neat steps, and every point had a date under it.

qa.q: How tall was the bean plant on the 5th?
How did Raghav feel about writing the numbers every morning?
qa.a: He felt sure it mattered and determined, because he did not want to guess at the fair.

qa.q: What else could Raghav add to his notebook, and why?
qa.a: He could note the weather or watering each day, because that might explain why growth was faster on some days.

qa.q: How does the daily measuring look to Salma?
qa.a: Salma first thinks it is unnecessary, then starts to see why dates and numbers matter when he explains.

grounding: It shows a boy measuring his plant each morning and noting it with the date so he has real numbers for his chart.

subtype: Approach: writing observations in a daily notebook [Action]
passage: For the science fair I grew a tomato seedling in a yoghurt cup on our windowsill. Every morning, before brushing my teeth, I held a ruler against the stem and wrote the height and the date in a small blue notebook. Some days it was boring. Some days it didn't grow at all, and I wrote 0 anyway. My friend Gautam said, "Bhai, just draw the graph on the last day." But at the end I didn't have to remember anything. I had twenty-one numbers with dates. When the judge asked when it grew fastest, I opened the notebook: days nine to twelve. She nodded and wrote something down. I think I, Raghav, grew a bit too.

qa.q: How many numbers did Raghav have at the end?
qa.a: Raghav had twenty-one numbers with dates.

qa.q: How did Raghav feel when the judge asked when it grew fastest?
qa.a: Raghav felt confident and proud, able to open the notebook and give a real answer.

qa.q: What else could Raghav try if he forgot to measure one day?
qa.a: Raghav could mark that day as missed rather than guess, so the chart stays honest.

qa.q: How might Gautam see the notebook after the fair?
qa.a: Gautam might realise that the boring daily notes gave Raghav real answers for the judge.

grounding: It shows a boy measuring his plant's height each morning and writing it with the date, which gives real numbers for his final chart.
